question: Can a continual topic model that carries a prior forward across time slices beat a sequential online LDA baseline on topic coherence and topic stability over a text stream?
method: Stratified 80/20 split of 20 Newsgroups; training part cut into 5 random time slices; sequential online LDA (20 topics) baseline with default priors vs an improved online LDA whose topic-word prior eta and per-slice prior-blend weight are chosen jointly by cross-validation on an inner split of the training data over eta in {default, 0.02, 0.05, 0.2} x mix in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75}; evaluated by NPMI on held-out test docs, stability and LR macro-F1; 3 seeds.
metric_name: NPMI topic coherence of top-10 words on held-out test documents
baseline: Standard sequential online LDA (sklearn LatentDirichletAllocation with default priors, partial_fit per slice, 20 topics); stand-in, not the paper's neural CoNTM.
improved: Same online LDA and slices, with the topic-word prior and a continual per-slice prior blend chosen by CV on training data only (grid includes the baseline setting). No extra data or extra fits on test.
notes: Topic stability compares index-aligned topics across consecutive slices. The improved model's hyperparameters (topic_word_prior eta and blend weight mix) are selected by a small inner CV on training data only (seed 42), run before the test evaluation; the grid contains the baseline setting, so the selected setting is never worse than the baseline on the validation split. Test-set gains are not guaranteed and are reported as measured. The 20 Newsgroups data has no timestamps, so random slices simulate a stream. Results are from a small seed count and a single data split.
